name: Anonymity & Censorship Resistance
description: Anonymous communication (Tor, mix nets) and tools to detect or circumvent censorship.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this area (2018) spans two fronts that would define the field: studying the privacy guarantees of deployed anonymity systems, and measuring censorship at scale. On the anonymity side, "An Empirical Analysis of Anonymity in Zcash" (2018) showed that even a system built for strong privacy leaks deanonymizing patterns in practice, while "How Do Tor Users Interact With Onion Services?" (2018) examined the human side of Tor's hidden services. On the censorship side, "Quack: Scalable Remote Measurement of Application-Layer Censorship" (2018) pushed remote measurement beyond DNS- and IP-level blocking, and "Effective Detection of Multimedia Protocol Tunneling using Machine Learning" (2018) foreshadowed an arms race in which machine learning would be wielded by both circumventers and censors.

Around 2019-2020 the focus shifted toward attacking and defending Tor at the network level. "Point Break: A Study of Bandwidth Denial-of-Service Attacks against Tor" (2019) probed how cheaply the network could be degraded, and traffic-analysis threats came to the foreground with "Zero-delay Lightweight Defenses against Website Fingerprinting" (2020), which sought practical fingerprinting defenses without latency cost. Meanwhile "Walking Onions: Scaling Anonymity Networks while Protecting Users" (2020) tackled the structural problem of growing an anonymity network without leaking differing views of it to attackers.

The 2021-2022 period broadened the threat model from Tor outward to VPNs and the broader transport layer, and made censorship circumvention more programmatic. "Blind In/On-Path Attacks and Applications to VPNs" (2021) and "Off-Path Network Traffic Manipulation via Revitalized ICMP Redirect Attacks" (2022) exposed how encrypted tunnels can be undermined from off-path, while a cluster of studies ("How and Why People Use Virtual Private Networks," 2022) examined what users actually expect from VPNs. Circumvention itself became automated and adversarial: "Balboa: Bobbing and Weaving around Network Censorship" (2021) and "GET /out: Automated Discovery of Application-Layer Censorship Evasion Strategies" (2022) treated evasion as a search problem, and "Online Website Fingerprinting" (2022) stress-tested fingerprinting attacks under realistic, open-world conditions.

By 2023-2024 the area matured into a tightly coupled measurement-and-circumvention arms race centered on real censors. "How the Great Firewall of China Detects and Blocks Fully Encrypted Traffic" (2023) reverse-engineered a nation-scale censor's actual classifier, "Subverting Website Fingerprinting Defenses with Robust Traffic Representation" (2023) showed deep-learning attacks defeating prior defenses, and "DeResistor: Toward Detection-Resistant Probing for Evasion of Internet Censorship" (2023) made probing itself stealthy. Deployment-oriented systems then took center stage with "Snowflake, a censorship circumvention system using temporary WebRTC proxies" (2024) and "SpotProxy: Rediscovering the Cloud for Censorship Circumvention" (2024), while "Bridging Barriers: A Survey of Challenges and Priorities in the Censorship Circumvention Landscape" (2024) stepped back to map the field's open problems.

milestones.title: Quack: Scalable Remote Measurement of Application-Layer Censorship
milestones.note: extended global censorship measurement beyond DNS/IP blocking to the application layer

milestones.title: An Empirical Analysis of Anonymity in Zcash
milestones.note: showed a privacy-focused cryptocurrency still leaks deanonymizing patterns in practice

milestones.title: Zero-delay Lightweight Defenses against Website Fingerprinting
milestones.note: advanced practical traffic-analysis defenses for Tor without imposing latency overhead

milestones.title: Balboa: Bobbing and Weaving around Network Censorship
milestones.note: introduced a general link-obfuscation framework, reframing circumvention as systematic evasion

milestones.title: Online Website Fingerprinting: Evaluating Website Fingerprinting Attacks on Tor in the Real World
milestones.note: stress-tested fingerprinting attacks under realistic open-world conditions rather than lab settings

milestones.title: How the Great Firewall of China Detects and Blocks Fully Encrypted Traffic
milestones.note: reverse-engineered a nation-scale censor's actual classifier for fully encrypted protocols

milestones.title: Subverting Website Fingerprinting Defenses with Robust Traffic Representation
milestones.note: demonstrated robust deep-learning fingerprinting that defeats prior state-of-the-art defenses

milestones.title: Snowflake, a censorship circumvention system using temporary WebRTC proxies
milestones.note: delivered a deployed, blocking-resistant circumvention system built on ephemeral volunteer proxies
